s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of involuntary movements in an elderly patient with a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
salient_findings: Involuntary movements of the left upper and lower limbs
Slow response and reduced muscle strength in the left limbs
Positive tendon reflexes in the left limbs
High-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on brain MRI
key_facts: The patient is an 80-year-old woman
She has a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
She presented with involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs for more than 10 days
She had a slow response on neurological examination
She had reduced muscle strength in her left limbs
She had positive tendon reflexes in her left limbs
Her blood glucose level was 8.59 mmol/L
Her hemoglobin A1c was 7.43%
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions
Brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Non-ketotic hyperglycemia-induced chorea
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus and presented with involuntary movements, which is consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Hyperglycemic hemiballism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's high blood glucose level and hemoglobin A1c, along with involuntary movements, make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Diabetic chorea
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus and presentation of involuntary movements are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Hemiballismus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's involuntary movements, particularly in the left arm and leg, are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Fahr disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's brain MRI showing high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia, along with involuntary movements, make this a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of involuntary movements, particularly the description of continuous, irregular movements of variable amplitude in the left arm and leg, combined with the history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus and the imaging findings, aligns with hyperglycemic hemiballism, a rare condition associated with hyperglycemia and characterized by hemiballistic movements.

rejected.label: Non-ketotic hyperglycemia-induced chorea
rejected.why: While the patient has hyperglycemia, the specific description of her movements and the localization to one side of the body are more suggestive of hemiballism than chorea.

rejected.label: Diabetic chorea
rejected.why: This term is less specific and does not fully capture the severity and nature of the patient's movement disorder, which is more accurately described as hemiballism.

rejected.label: Hemiballismus
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms include hemiballistic movements, the term 'hyperglycemic hemiballism' more accurately reflects the etiological link to her hyperglycemia.

rejected.label: Fahr disease
rejected.why: Fahr disease is characterized by bilateral basal ganglia calcification and does not typically present with acute onset of hemiballistic movements in the context of hyperglycemia.
